code: OSS-Fuzz report for capstone fuzz_disasmnext: X86 Intel printer crash state printOperand -> X86_Intel_printInst -> cs_disasm
note: Identifies the vulnerable path as x86 Intel disassembly/printing, with the attacker-controlled bytes reaching the printer through cs_disasm.
This raw byte sequence is the attacker-controlled input used to trigger the bug in the regression reproducer.
cs_disasm allocates the instruction/detail output object that will later be populated by the printer, establishing the sink object for the malformed instruction state.
The printer writes memory-operand fields while walking decoded operands; the crash report points here because the operand bookkeeping can become inconsistent for the crafted x86 input.
The printer fetches an operand from the decoded MCInst and branches on its kind; the attacker-controlled instruction bytes determine which operand path is taken.
For register operands, the printer reads the register value and uses it to populate detail metadata; if the operand state is malformed, this propagates bad state into the detail structure.

The root cause is that the printer assumes the current detail slot is valid and initialized; the crafted input drives a path where the printer consumes or exposes uninitialized operand state, leading to the MSAN use-of-uninitialized-value in printOperand/X86_Intel_printInst/cs_disasm.
